title: Verification Asymmetries in AI Safety Commitments
bottleneck: AI labs' safety commitments are largely self-reported, and independent evaluators lack the access needed to verify training practices, incident handling, or safeguard effectiveness. The Future of Life Institute's 2025 AI Safety Index gave no leading company above a C+ overall, with existential safety planning scoring worst. Companies control what evaluators see, and competitive pressure rewards minimal disclosure.
why_it_blocks: Unverifiable commitments are indistinguishable from marketing, so the public cannot tell which labs are actually safe. Trust without verification leaves the public unable to distinguish genuine safety from theater.
current_state: Embedded third-party evaluator proposals (Amodei's 2026 plan, endorsed by rival CEOs) are the leading fix, but none is yet operational with real access. Making evaluator access a licensing condition is the proposed remedy, but no government has imposed it.
